subject: Intermittent token spikes in long-lived sessions — how are they billed?
messages:
From: Jason Li <jason.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Metering question: long-lived session w/ intermittent spikes

Hi Elliot,

Quick question as we're finalizing the SOW: our clinical assistant runs persistent sessions per user (session lives for days) but traffic is bursty — most minutes are idle with occasional 10s-40s token bursts when clinicians paste long notes. How will those intermittent spikes be billed under the proposed per-token model + session minimum? Specifically:

- Do you count every burst token individually, or do you aggregate by session window?
- Is there any smoothing or a minimum basket per minute that would inflate our bill for idle minutes?
- Will KV/prefix caching reduce charges when prompts reuse the same context across bursts?

Attached is a 48-hour sample log (session_sample_log.csv) showing the pattern. We're trying to estimate monthly spend for 10k active clinicians.

Thanks,
Jason
Jason Li
Director, Integrations
Acme Health
From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Li <jason.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Metering question: long-lived session w/ intermittent spikes

Jason — thanks for the sample, this is exactly the kind of pattern we see in health workflows. Short answers up front, then details:

1) We bill per-token for tokens actually consumed by generation/embedding calls. We do not bill idle wall-clock time.

2) To avoid extreme bill volatility from tiny bursts, we apply a per-request rounding quantum (configurable per-account). By default we round each request up to 32 token units. That means a 3-token burst will be billed as 32 tokens unless you opt into micro-billing.

3) Long-lived sessions themselves do not incur a continuous charge, but KV/prefix caching reduces repeated prompt tokens when you reuse context — cached tokens are not re-sent to the model and therefore not re-billed as input tokens. Billing still counts newly generated tokens.

Given your scale, I recommend three levers: increase the rounding quantum to smooth spikes (if you want predictable per-minute floors), enable prefix caching aggressively, and consider a reserved capacity plan with a committed monthly token pool (we can apply a discount at commit).

I'm looping in Vanessa and Priyom from sales/finance to propose a tailored pricing construct and run cost simulations against your log.

—Elliot
Elliot Price
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Metering question: long-lived session w/ intermittent spikes

Elliot — forwarding the log. Quick notes for pricing brainstorm:

- Option A (default): per-token billing + 32-token request quantum + standard prefix caching. Predictable but billing will show many small quanta for 3–10 token bursts.

- Option B (smoothing): apply 5-minute aggregation windows for the account where we sum tokens per session across the window and round once to the quantum. This way a handful of tiny bursts in 5 minutes are aggregated and billed once.

  Pros: reduces noise, lower invoice variance.
  Cons: slightly higher peak risk for abuse; requires monitoring and anti-abuse thresholds.

- Option C (commit): committed monthly token pool (e.g., 100M tokens) with blended discount and roll-over credit for unused. Best for predictability given 10k clinicians.

Questions for Priyom/Marissa: how would we price Option B for a mid-market commitment? We should include an anti-abuse clause and a dashboard metric for 5-min aggregate usage per session.

Vanessa
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Metering question: long-lived session w/ intermittent spikes

Vanessa / Elliot — quick commercial proposal to move the thread forward so Jason has numbers:

- Pilot pricing (3 months): we implement 5-minute aggregation windows for the account (Option B) and set the rounding quantum to 16 tokens for the pilot.
- Pilot token pool: 20M tokens committed, billed monthly at a 12% discount versus list per-token.
- After pilot: go to a committed plan sized off observed 30-day usage with blended discounts (15–25% depending on commit band).
- Abuse guard: we add a rate ceiling per session (tokens per minute) and a monitoring alert. If ceiling exceeded for sustained periods, we flag for review and may meter at per-request quantum rather than aggregated window.

I'll prepare a short one-pager and an updated SLA usage matrix (attached) that documents the billing behavior and the anti-abuse policy. If that looks good, Elliot — can you get a quick signal from Jason on whether Acme prefers pilot or straight commit?

—Priyom
